description: Lamb Ouzi is a magnificent Middle Eastern feast, traditionally featuring tender, slow-roasted lamb atop a bed of aromatic spiced rice. This recipe brings the rich flavors of ouzi to your table, combining fluffy rice with succulent lamb pieces and toasted nuts. It is a celebratory dish perfect for sharing with family and friends.

instructions.title: Prepare Rice and Aromatics
instructions.text: Rinse the Basmati rice thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear. Drain well and set aside. Finely chop the onion and mince the garlic. Prepare your shredded or cubed pre-cooked lamb.

instructions.title: Sauté Spices and Onion
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat ghee or olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the minced garlic, Seven Spice, ground cinnamon, ground cardamom, and nutmeg. Cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Cook the Spiced Rice
instructions.text: Add the rinsed Basmati rice to the pot with the spices and onion. Stir well to coat the rice grains. Pour in the hot chicken or lamb broth and add the bay leaves. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until all the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.

instructions.title: Incorporate Lamb and Peas
instructions.text: Once the rice is cooked, gently fold in the shredded pre-cooked lamb and thawed frozen peas. Cover the pot again and let it sit off the heat for 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the lamb and peas to warm through.

instructions.title: Prepare Toasted Nuts
instructions.text: While the rice is resting, toast the slivered almonds and pine nuts. In a small dry skillet, toast the nuts over medium-low heat, stirring frequently, until golden brown and fragrant. Be careful not to burn them, as they can toast quickly.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish
instructions.text: Remove the bay leaves from the rice. Fluff the Ouzi rice gently with a fork. Transfer the Lamb Ouzi to a large serving platter. Garnish generously with the toasted slivered almonds, pine nuts, and freshly chopped parsley. Serve immediately as a magnificent centerpiece.

tips: For an authentic Middle Eastern flavor, use a good quality Seven Spice blend (Baharat). You can find it in most Middle Eastern grocery stores or online.
The success of this recipe relies on tender, pre-cooked lamb. If preparing lamb from scratch, slow roast a shoulder or leg until fall-apart tender, then shred it for best results.
For a richer flavor, consider layering the Ouzi in a large oven-safe dish and baking it briefly before serving to ensure everything is piping hot and infused with aroma.
article:
Unveiling the majestic centerpiece of Middle Eastern celebrations, Lamb Ouzi Whole Slow Roasted is more than just a meal; it's an experience. This iconic dish, with its tender, fall-off-the-bone lamb, aromatic spiced rice, and a medley of toasted nuts, embodies the warmth, generosity, and rich culinary heritage of the region. Perfect for festive gatherings, family reunions, or any occasion demanding a show-stopping dish, preparing a whole slow-roasted Lamb Ouzi is a labor of love that promises unforgettable flavors and a truly impressive presentation. Get ready to embark on a culinary journey that will transform your dining table into a Middle Eastern feast.

## What is Lamb Ouzi?

Lamb Ouzi, often spelled "Qoozi" or "Ghozi," is a quintessential Middle Eastern dish renowned for its grandeur and deliciousness. At its heart, it features a whole lamb or a substantial cut like a shoulder or leg, slow-roasted to absolute perfection until it's incredibly tender and juicy. The star of the show isn't just the lamb; it's traditionally served atop a generous bed of fragrant, spiced Basmati rice, often studded with toasted nuts like pine nuts and almonds, and sometimes green peas. This dish is a staple at weddings, Eid celebrations, and other significant family gatherings, symbolizing hospitality and abundance. The preparation of Lamb Ouzi is an art form, a testament to patience and a deep understanding of spices, resulting in a symphony of flavors that is both complex and comforting. While variations exist, the essence remains the same: a magnificent celebration of slow-cooked lamb and aromatic rice.

## Ingredients for Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi

To create an authentic and unforgettable Lamb Ouzi, selecting high-quality ingredients is paramount. The journey begins with the star:

*   **The Lamb:** A whole lamb shoulder (4-6 lbs) or a leg of lamb (5-7 lbs) is ideal. Look for well-marbled meat for maximum flavor and tenderness.
*   **For the Lamb Marinade:**
    *   1 head garlic, cloves peeled and crushed
    *   2 large onions, roughly chopped
    *   1/4 cup olive oil
    *   1/4 cup lemon juice
    *   2 tablespoons Middle Eastern Seven Spice blend (or a mix of cumin, coriander, cardamom, cinnamon, black pepper, nutmeg, cloves)
    *   1 tablespoon turmeric powder
    *   1 tablespoon sweet paprika
    *   1 teaspoon black pepper
    *   Salt to taste (generous amount for a large cut)
    *   Optional: A few sprigs of fresh rosemary or thyme for aroma.
*   **For the Spiced Rice:**
    *   3 cups Basmati rice, soaked for 30 minutes and drained
    *   1 large onion, finely chopped
    *   2-3 tablespoons ghee or butter
    *   4 cups lamb or chicken broth (or water)
    *   1 tablespoon Middle Eastern Seven Spice blend
    *   1 teaspoon turmeric powder
    *   1/2 teaspoon ground cardamom
    *   Salt and black pepper to taste
    *   1 cup frozen green peas (optional)
*   **For Garnish:**
    *   1/2 cup pine nuts
    *   1/2 cup slivered almonds
    *   2 tablespoons olive oil or ghee (for toasting nuts)
    *   Fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish

These ingredients, when combined with care and patience, will lay the foundation for a truly spectacular Lamb Ouzi.

## Step-by-Step Guide to Making Lamb Ouzi

Crafting a whole slow-roasted Lamb Ouzi is a rewarding process that unfolds in several key stages, each contributing to its legendary flavor and tenderness.

1.  **Prepare the Lamb Marinade:** In a food processor, combine the crushed garlic, chopped onions, olive oil, lemon juice, seven spice blend, turmeric, paprika, black pepper, and salt. Process until a thick paste forms.
2.  **Marinate the Lamb:** Pat the lamb dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, make several deep incisions all over the lamb. Rub the marinade generously over the entire surface, ensuring it penetrates the cuts. For best results, cover and refrigerate overnight, or for a minimum of 4-6 hours. This allows the flavors to deeply infuse and tenderize the meat.
3.  **Slow Roast the Lamb:** Preheat your oven to a low temperature, around 300°F (150°C). Place the marinated lamb in a large roasting pan. Add about 1-2 cups of water or broth to the bottom of the pan to create steam and prevent drying. Cover the pan tightly with foil, ensuring no steam escapes. Roast for 4-6 hours, or until the lamb is incredibly tender and easily pulls away from the bone. The exact time will depend on the size and cut of your lamb. Periodically check the liquid in the pan and replenish if needed.
4.  **Rest the Lamb:** Once roasted, remove the lamb from the oven and keep it covered with foil. Let it rest for at least 30 minutes before carving or shredding. This crucial step allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring a succulent and flavorful result.
5.  **Prepare the Spiced Rice:** While the lamb is resting, prepare the rice. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the ghee or butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the seven spice blend, turmeric, and cardamom, cooking for another minute until fragrant. Add the drained Basmati rice and stir to coat evenly with the spices. Pour in the lamb or chicken broth, season with salt and pepper, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until all the liquid is absorbed and the rice is fluffy. If using, stir in the green peas during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
6.  **Toast the Nuts:** In a small skillet, heat the olive oil or ghee over medium heat. Add the pine nuts and almonds and toast until golden brown, stirring constantly to prevent burning. Remove from heat immediately.
7.  **Assemble and Serve:** On a large serving platter, spread the spiced rice evenly. Gently place the whole slow-roasted Lamb Ouzi on top of the rice. Garnish generously with the toasted pine nuts and almonds, and a sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley. Present the entire dish at the table for a truly spectacular reveal.

## Expert Tips for Tender Lamb Ouzi

Achieving that melt-in-your-mouth tenderness in your Lamb Ouzi is the hallmark of a truly successful dish. Here are some expert tips to ensure your lamb is as succulent as possible:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the lamb sits in the aromatic spice mixture, the more deeply the flavors will penetrate, and the enzymes in the lemon juice and onions will work to tenderize the meat. Overnight is ideal.
*   **Low and Slow is the Way to Go:** Resist the urge to rush the roasting process. A low oven temperature (300°F / 150°C) over a long period breaks down the tough connective tissues in the lamb, resulting in incredibly tender meat. High heat will dry it out before it becomes tender.
*   **Keep it Covered:** Tightly covering your roasting pan with foil creates a steamy environment, essentially braising the lamb in its own juices and the added liquid. This prevents the lamb from drying out and helps it cook evenly. Only uncover for the last 30-60 minutes if you desire a slightly crispier exterior.
*   **Add Moisture to the Pan:** Always ensure there's some liquid (water or broth) at the bottom of the roasting pan. This not only keeps the lamb moist but also provides a flavorful base for basting.
*   **Don't Forget to Rest:** This is a non-negotiable step for any roasted meat. Resting allows the muscle fibers to relax and reabsorb the juices that have migrated to the center during cooking. Skipping this step will result in dry, less flavorful lamb.
*   **For Extra Flavor:** Consider adding some bone broth or lamb stock to your roasting pan instead of water for an even richer pan sauce.

## Serving Suggestions for Your Ouzi Feast

A grand dish like Lamb Ouzi deserves to be presented as the centerpiece of a magnificent feast. The traditional way is to serve the whole slow-roasted lamb directly on top of the spiced rice on a very large, ornate platter, allowing guests to admire its splendor before serving.

*   **Accompaniments:**
    *   **Yogurt Sauce (Labneh or Tzatziki):** A cool, tangy yogurt sauce, perhaps with cucumber, garlic, and mint, provides a refreshing counterpoint to the rich lamb and rice.
    *   **Simple Green Salad:** A light salad dressed with lemon and olive oil offers freshness and cuts through the richness.
    *   **Pickled Vegetables (Torshi):** Various Middle Eastern pickles add a delightful sour and briny crunch.
    *   **Extra Toasted Nuts:** Have a small bowl of extra toasted pine nuts and almonds on the side for guests who want more crunch.
    *   **Fresh Herbs:** A platter of fresh mint, parsley, and cilantro can be offered for a burst of herbaceous flavor.
*   **Beverages:** Offer traditional Middle Eastern mint tea, or refreshing fruit juices like apricot or tamarind. For a more celebratory touch, a good quality red wine can also pair beautifully with the rich lamb.
*   **Communal Dining:** The essence of Lamb Ouzi is communal sharing. Encourage guests to gather around the table and enjoy the experience together, sharing stories and laughter. This dish is designed to bring people together, making it more than just a meal, but a memorable event.

## Variations and Substitutions for Lamb Ouzi

While the classic whole slow-roasted Lamb Ouzi is a masterpiece, there are many ways to adapt it to your preferences, dietary needs, or the availability of ingredients.

*   **Meat Alternatives:** If a whole lamb shoulder or leg is too much, or if you prefer a different cut, lamb shanks or even bone-in lamb chops can be slow-cooked in a similar spiced broth until tender. For those who don't eat lamb, beef short ribs or a beef chuck roast can be used, though the flavor profile will naturally shift.
*   **Rice Variations:** Basmati rice is traditional, but long-grain rice varieties like Jasmine can also be used. For a different texture, some recipes incorporate a mix of rice and vermicelli. You can also vary the spices in the rice, perhaps adding more cinnamon for sweetness or a touch of saffron for color and aroma.
*   **Spice Adjustments:** The Middle Eastern Seven Spice blend is a common base, but you can adjust it to your taste. Some regions might favor more turmeric, others more cardamom, or even a hint of dried lime powder (loomi) for a tangy note. Experiment to find your perfect balance.
*   **Vegetable Additions:** Beyond green peas, you can stir in finely diced carrots, bell peppers, or even a handful of dried cranberries or raisins into the rice for extra sweetness and texture.
*   **Stuffed Ouzi (Lamb Stuffed with Rice):** A more elaborate variation involves deboning a lamb shoulder and stuffing the spiced rice directly inside the cavity before roasting. This method ensures the rice absorbs even more of the lamb's juices and flavor.
*   **Nut and Garnish Diversity:** While pine nuts and almonds are classic, walnuts or pistachios can also be used for garnish. For a touch of color and acidity, pomegranate seeds make a beautiful and delicious addition to the finished dish.

Embracing these variations allows you to put your unique spin on this ancient and cherished recipe, ensuring that your Lamb Ouzi remains a beloved dish for every occasion.
